titulo: The past with «être» and reflexive verbs: Telling about a trip

aula.titulo: The past with «être» and reflexive verbs
aula.objetivo: Use the passé composé with «être» (verbs of movement and reflexive verbs), make the participle agree, and tell about a trip.

blocos.titulo: Avoir or être? A practical rule
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: use «être» with the verbs of movement and change on the list and with all reflexive verbs. STEP 2: use «avoir» with all the others, and with verbs that have a direct object: «J'ai pris le train.» «J'ai visité Paris.» STEP 3: some verbs change auxiliary when they have an object: «Je suis sorti» (no object) but «J'ai sorti la voiture» (with an object). STEP 4: «descendre», «monter», «rentrer», «sortir»: with an object, they use «avoir». STEP 5: when in doubt, ask: «is there a direct object?» If so, «avoir».
blocos.comparacao: in English one auxiliary, «have», does everything. French makes you choose: «être» for movement and for reflexive verbs, «avoir» for the rest. Most verbs use «avoir».

blocos.titulo: Un voyage à Lyon / A trip to Lyon
blocos.ru: Samedi dernier, je suis allé à Lyon avec ma sœur. Nous sommes partis à sept heures et nous sommes arrivés à neuf heures. Nous avons pris un café à la gare. Puis nous avons visité la ville. Le soir, nous sommes rentrés fatigués mais très contents.
blocos.pt: Last Saturday, I went to Lyon with my sister. We left at seven o'clock and arrived at nine. We had a coffee at the station. Then we visited the city. In the evening, we came back tired but very happy.

blocos.enunciado: Tell about a real or imaginary trip, using «être» and «avoir» in the past.
Say: «Elle s'est levée à sept heures. Nous nous sommes couchés tard.»
